payload.headline: Meta rebounds 3.4% to 609.89 into resistance; still waiting for the 2027-01-27 report

summary.thesis: Sales are still growing fast, but margins and free cash flow have dropped sharply, and at 609.89 the price already assumes a strong recovery in cash flow.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait. Swing: no trade, because the bounce stopped just under resistance and the trend is still down.
summary.act_at: Buy at 475.85; no swing trade until a close above 626.86

payload.happening: Meta rose 3.4% to 609.89. That takes it out of the 592.87–607.98 support zone and up to the bottom of the 611.95–626.54 resistance zone. The trend is still a downtrend: the 20-day average (615.27) is falling and the price is below both the 50-day (672.4) and 200-day (626.86) averages. TechCrunch reported two small product updates: scheduled messages on WhatsApp, and a vertical-video update for creators at X, a competitor. The next earnings report is on 2027-01-27.
payload.business: Demand is not the problem. Trailing sales grew 27.53% to 241.6B, and gross margin is 81.03%. However, quarterly growth has slowed from 33.08% two quarters ago to 26.07%. The real issue is cost. Operating margin (the share of sales left after running costs) fell from 43.23% to 32.86%. Free cash flow (cash left after spending on the business) fell from 44.8B to 28.6B, so only 11.86% of sales now turns into free cash. The filings also flag that profit per share is trailing sales and that the company missed forecasts by 29% last quarter. The balance sheet is not at risk: liquidity is 82.4B and net cash is close to zero at -1.2B, even with 83.7B of debt. Today's news only affects sentiment. A scheduling feature and a rival's video update do not change demand, margins or cash. The $14.1M of insider sales outside pre-set plans is a governance signal, not a business change. What is at risk is cash generation and margins. Revenue and financial stability are not.

worth.text: The methods disagree because they rest on different assumptions. A discounted-cash-flow model (DCF) values the business on its future cash, starting from today's 28.6B and using a 9.9% discount rate. It gives 244.22 (bear), 379.4 (base) and 517.42 (bull). All three are below 609.89. To justify today's price, free cash flow would have to start growing at about 36.7% a year. Even 30% growth gives only 476.95. Meta's own price-to-sales history gives a much higher range of 475.85–707.21–881.21, because it assumes the market will pay what it usually has relative to sales. On simple multiples the stock is not expensive. It trades at 20.9 times trailing earnings and 6.5 times sales, close to the peer median of 6.1 and at the 30th percentile of its own 5-year range. Cash flow is what separates the two approaches. If margins kept shrinking, the value would fall further: 244.63 at a 24% operating margin. My fair-value range is 475.85–707.21. The current price sits inside it, but only if cash flow recovers.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow recovers toward the earlier 44.8B as the heavy spending pays off, instead of staying near 28.6B.

bull: Sales are still growing 27.53% a year on a 241.6B base, and gross margin is 81.03%, so customer demand looks intact.
Relative to sales, the stock is cheap compared with its own past: price-to-sales of 6.5 is at the 30th percentile of its 5-year range, and the history mid-point is 707.21.
The balance sheet is solid: liquidity is 82.4B and net cash is only -1.2B, so the spending cycle does not put the company at risk.
bear: Free cash flow fell from 44.8B to 28.6B, and today's price implies 36.7% starting cash-flow growth, above the highest DCF value of 517.42.
Operating margin fell from 43.23% to 32.86%. A further drop to 24% would cut the DCF value to 244.63.
The price trend is down. The price is below the 50-day average of 672.4 and the 200-day average of 626.86, and the 20-day average of 615.27 is still falling.

levels.what: Bottom of the lower support zone (576.61–591.58). A close below it would mean the downtrend has resumed after today's bounce.
The DCF bull value. Below it, the price no longer sits above every cash-flow estimate.
Buy level: the low end of Meta's own price-to-sales history and close to the 476.95 value at 30% growth, so buying here does not depend on a full margin recovery.

longterm.why: At 609.89 the price is above every DCF value, the business is graded C, and free cash flow is shrinking. Buying now would mean paying in advance for a recovery that the reports have not yet shown.

swing.why: The bounce stopped at the bottom of the 611.95–626.54 resistance zone, with the falling 20-day average (615.27) and the 200-day average (626.86) just overhead. The average daily move (ATR) is 25.35, so that zone could absorb a single day's move. No trade until a close above 626.86.

decision.timing: Options price a 9.4% move by Dec 18 and a 17.9% move by Feb 19, a window that includes the 2027-01-27 report. That report settles the cash-flow question, so there is no long-term entry before it unless the price reaches 475.85 first.

change_mind: The 2027-01-27 report shows free cash flow rising above 28.6B and operating margin moving back toward 43.23%. That would support the 707.21 history value and justify buying above 475.85.
A close above 641.9, the top of the upper resistance zone, with the 20-day average no longer falling. That would end the downtrend and open a swing entry.
Operating margin falls toward 24%, where the DCF value is 244.63. That would change the long-term action from wait to avoid, even at 475.85.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait, because today's 3.4% rise to 609.89 leaves the price above every DCF value (the highest is 517.42) and it stopped right at resistance.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
